question: Rama experiences a drop in temperature as she is getting higher and higher in the mountains while trekking. What could be the cause of this?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lower air pressure at altitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As altitude increases, the **air pressure** decreases.
 
• Lower air pressure at higher altitudes causes the air to be less dense.
 
• Less dense air holds less heat, leading to a **drop in temperature**.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the **lapse rate**, where the temperature decreases with an increase in altitude.
 
• The average lapse rate in the troposphere is about **6.5°C per 1000 meters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Higher air pressure at altitude**__

 __
 
• At higher altitudes, air pressure actually decreases, not increases.
 
• Higher air pressure is found at lower altitudes, closer to sea level.
 
 
 
• **Rama's fatigue**__
 __
 
• While fatigue can affect one's perception of temperature, it is not the primary cause of temperature drop at higher altitudes.
 
 
 
• **Less water**__
 
 
• Dehydration can affect body temperature regulation, but it is not related to the environmental temperature change at higher altitudes.
